findings.issue: Rating bounds check uses && instead of ||, so it can never reject an invalid value — any integer rating (e.g. 9999 or -50) passes validation and is persisted.
findings.evidence: if (!Number.isInteger(rating) || (rating < 1 && rating > 5)) { ... } — the clause (rating < 1 && rating > 5) is always false.

findings.issue: SQL injection: the `sort` parameter from `GET /books/:id/reviews?sort=` is interpolated unsanitized into the ORDER BY clause, unlike the sibling getBooksPage which whitelists its sort column.
findings.evidence: ORDER BY ${sort} in getReviewsSorted, fed directly from `const sort = (req.query.sort as string) || 'r.created_at DESC';` in src/routes/api.ts.

findings.issue: Stored XSS: display_name is rendered into an HTML response via raw template-string res.send() with no escaping, unlike sibling routes that use the res.render templating engine.
findings.evidence:
res.send(`
${top.display_name} rated it ${top.rating}/5
`) — display_name is set unsanitized at user creation (api.ts).
